newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - U.S. June T-bonds hover near key support.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - U.S. June T-bonds hover near key support.

text.p: U.S. June T-bonds hovered near key support as the market took a breather from continuing its long-term downtrend, technical analysts said.
June fell to 108-08/32, which is roughly equivalent to the long bond yield's key psychological resistance level of seven percent.
"It looks like it's stabilizing over the short term," Robert Zukowski, a technical analyst with MCM MoneyWatch, said on Reuters Financial Television on Wednesday morning.
He said oversold indicators point to a period of sideways trade before breaking lower.
Some Eurodollar floor analysts noted, however, that prices for September and December broke through key support levels despite extremely oversold readings on relative strength indices (RSI).
"Everyone is just ignoring the RSIs," one Eurodollar futures analyst said after September and December set new lows for the year on heavy dealer selling.

September Eurodollars fell through 93.75, retracing 50 percent of their July-December move, and are expected to test 93.66. September would be pricing in another 25-basis-point rate hike if it fell to 93.66, one floor trader said.
"The game changed yesterday," James Bianco, director of research at Arbor Trading Group, Inc, said about the Federal Open Market Committee's decision to raise a key interest rate by 25 basis points.
Several analysts pointed out that June bonds' rally late Tuesday failed to take the contract through key resistance.
"We stalled just below the 200-day moving average of 109-27/32," Zukowski said.
June T-bonds rose to 109-25/32, the 1-1/2-week high, in an immediate reaction to the FOMC's rate announcement on Tuesday.
"Yesterday's high now takes on added importance," Stewart Taylor, an analyst with Taylor Fixed-Income Outlook, wrote in his daily newsletter.
Taylor said the contract's disintegration at 109-25/32 and close below the morning pivot were bearish.
"Bonds closed in the lower portion of a fairly wide daily price spread on strong volume," Taylor wrote.
Taylor said a close above 109-25/32 would set the stage for a stronger correction.
"I don't see a real threat (to the upside) at this point in time," Zukowski said.
Technical analysts also noted that the decline in total bond futures open interest confirmed strong liquidation pressures.
While bond futures open interest rose on Tuesday, the number of open positions has fallen since February 26 when open interest set a record high of 579,445.
"Greenspan was speaking that day, and the perception at that point was that nothing was going to happen," Bianco said. (Chicago DerivativesDesk 312-408-8750))
